text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.

For the Fisk Jubilee Singers' book of 1872, George L. White took the words down from the singers, and Theodore F. Seward wrote the music down; every melody was tested on the piano, and no line or phrase went in without the singers' full endorsement.

source.en: Theodore F. Seward, Jubilee Songs (Biglow & Main, New York, 1872), introduction, read from the scan

Record the tune of Didn't My Lord Deliver Daniel in Sing, with the other parts playing.
Seward noted that more than half the Fisk melodies use the scale of Scottish music, without its fourth and seventh notes. Didn't My Lord Deliver Daniel is one of them: its tune uses only five notes.

source.en: Theodore F. Seward, Jubilee Songs (1872), preface, p. 3, read from the scan; the song's notes, pp. 16 and 17
